name: Sarson ka Saag
subtitle: slow-cooked mustard greens, bitter and buttery, thickened with a little coarse flour

ingredients.qty: 750g, thick stalks removed and leaves roughly chopped

ingredients.note: softens the bitterness of the mustard
stirred in at the end to thicken the saag

ingredients.qty: 2 inch, half chopped and half julienned

prepNotes: Wash the greens in three changes of water — mustard leaves hold a lot of grit in the crinkles.
Strip the leaves off any stalk thicker than a pencil; those stalks stay stringy however long you cook them.
Mix the flour with 4 tbsp cold water to a smooth slurry before it goes near the pot, or it will go lumpy.

steps.text: Put the mustard greens, spinach, methi, chopped ginger, garlic, green chillies, 1 tsp salt and 1.5 cups water in the pressure cooker and cook 15 minutes at full pressure.
Let the pressure drop, then uncover — the greens should be army-green and completely collapsed.
Blend to a coarse puree, or crush with a wooden masher for the traditional rough texture.
steps.tip: Do not blend it smooth. Saag should have a slight grain to it.

steps.text: Return the puree to the pan and bring to a bare simmer.
Whisk in the flour slurry in a thin stream and cook 25 minutes on low, stirring every few minutes.
steps.tip: This long simmer is what turns raw bitterness into something round and sweet. Do not shorten it.

steps.text: Meanwhile heat the ghee in a small pan and fry the chopped onion until golden brown, about 8 minutes.
Add the julienned ginger to the onion and fry 1 minute more.
Pour the tempering into the saag, scraping the pan clean, and simmer 10 minutes more.
Taste for salt — greens need more than you expect — and finish with the butter melting on top.

storage: Keeps 4 days refrigerated and genuinely improves for the first two. Reheat slowly with a splash of water and fresh butter. Freezes 3 months.
